verses.commentary: When Israel was a child, I loved him. Parental language. God as father to the infant nation. Out of Egypt I called my son. The exodus as adoption. Matthew 2:15 applies this to Jesus coming out of Egypt. Israel's story becomes Christ's story.
The more they were called, the more they went away. Calling produces fleeing. They sacrificed to the Baals. The chronic disease. Burned incense to images. Worship misdirected.
It was I who taught Ephraim to walk. A toddler learning steps. Taking them by the arms. The father steadying the child. But they did not realize it was I who healed them. Unrecognized care.

I led them with cords of human kindness, with ties of love. Not harsh control but gentle guidance. To them I was like one who lifts a child to the cheek. Tender affection. I bent down to feed them. The parent stooping to the child's level.
Will they not return to Egypt? Exile threatened. Will not Assyria rule over them? The actual captor. Because they refuse to repent. The reason stated plainly.
A sword will flash in their cities. War within the gates. Devour their false prophets. The lying voices silenced. Put an end to their plans. Schemes terminated.
My people are determined to turn from me. Resolute rebellion. Even though they call me God Most High. Right title, wrong heart. I will by no means exalt them. They call him high but remain low.

How can I give you up, Ephraim? The divine struggle. How can I hand you over, Israel? The father's anguish. How can I treat you like Admah? The cities destroyed with Sodom (Deuteronomy 29:23). How can I make you like Zeboyim? Another destroyed city. My heart is changed within me. God's inner turmoil. All my compassion is aroused. Mercy stirring.

I will not carry out my fierce anger. Restraint. Nor will I devastate Ephraim again. Mercy prevails. For I am God, and not a man. Divine freedom to forgive. The Holy One among you. Presence for salvation. I will not come against their cities. Judgment suspended.

They will follow the Lord. Future restoration. He will roar like a lion. The same lion image, now calling home. When he roars, his children will come trembling from the west. The roar that scattered now gathers.

They will come from Egypt, trembling like sparrows. From the place of refuge. From Assyria, fluttering like doves. From the place of exile. I will settle them in their homes. Return completed. Restoration achieved.

Ephraim has surrounded me with lies. The present reality after the future vision. Israel with deceit. Still in deception. Judah is unruly against God. The southern kingdom also rebellious. Even against the faithful Holy One. Against God's faithfulness they are faithless.
